In a four-set of type 2+1+1 that could be newly admitted, either an undeleted triangle remains (doubled affected part) or the third part supplies both vertices of an undeleted four-cycle. Four occupied parts leave a triangle. Before the fault, the pairwise tetrahedral boundaries attach to the representative graph with pendants along trees, so they give independent primitive sphere factors. In the relative complex the single 3-cell attaches by the fundamental class of the affected pair boundary, and the two new 2-cells per third part map to the same fundamental cycle in the complete representative graph for its star spanning tree. Their differences lift to the displayed unfilled tetrahedral boundaries, because the other two triangles are old. This proves exactly the stated integral kernels, cokernels and generators. For the absolute target type the two old triangles form a disk giving an actual path homotopy, not just a homology. Collapse the representative triangle-edge pairs in the graph-plus-disks part of the homotopy model, not across the attached sphere pieces. Remaining new disks attach by null loops. At m=2 only the fill occurs. The packaged finite checks are consistent but not needed for the uniform conclusion.
